12. TERM / TENURE

The term / tenure of the Directors shall be governed as per provisions of the applicable laws, as amended from time to time and as follows: -

1. Managing Director / Whole-time Director / Manager (Managerial Person): -

The Company shall appoint or re-appoint any person as its Managerial Person for a term up to five years at a time. No re-appointment shall be made earlier than one year before the expiry of term.

2. Independent Director: -

An Independent Director may hold office for a term up to five consecutive years on the Board of the Company and will be eligible for re-appointment on passing of a special resolution by the Company and disclosure of such appointment in the Board's report.

No Independent Director shall hold office for more than two consecutive terms, however, such Independent Director shall be eligible for appointment after expiry of three years of ceasing to become an Independent Director. Provided that an Independent Director shall not, during the said period of three years, be appointed in or be associated with the Company in any other capacity, either directly or indirectly.

13. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION

The Committee shall specify the manner for effective evaluation of performance of the Board, its Committees and individual directors of the Company with the aim to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the Board and Committees.

The Board of Directors shall carry out the performance evaluation of every individual director except the director being evaluated, along with its various Board Committees and Board as whole. Further, performance evaluation shall be carried out at least once in a year in accordance with the manner prescribed in Annexure 2 hereto.

The performance evaluation of KMPs (excluding executive directors) shall be performed by Nomination & Remuneration Committee and of SMPs by the Compensation Committee of the Company, on annual basis or at the time of salary appraisals and in compliance with the Articles of Association of the Company.

14. POLICY ON DIVERSITY OF THE BOARD

a. The Company acknowledges the importance of diversity at the Board. Diversity encompasses diversity of perspective, experience, education, background, ethnicity and personal attributes. The Company recognizes that gender diversity is a significant aspect of diversity and acknowledges the role that woman with skills and experience can play in contributing to diversity of perspective at the Board. Other relevant matters such as independence and the ability to fulfil required time commitments in the case of Independent and Non-Executive Directors will also be taken into account;

<!-- image -->

b. The Committee shall review and evaluate Board composition to ensure that the Board have the appropriate mix of skills, experience, independence and knowledge to ensure their continued effectiveness. The Committee will ensure that no person is discriminated against on grounds of religion, race, gender, national origin or ancestry, marital status, age, or any other personal or physical attribute as a Board member; and
c. To ensure Board diversity at broad level, the Company shall provide sufficient information to the shareholders about the qualifications, expertise and characteristics of each Board Member.

15. REMOVAL / RETIREMENT

Owning to reasons for any disqualification mentioned in the applicable law, the Committee may recommend to the Board with reasons recorded in writing, removal of a Director and KMP subject to the provisions and compliance of the Applicable Law.

The Director and KMP shall retire as per the provisions of the applicable law and in accordance with the Human Resource Policy of the Company. The Board will have the discretion to retain the Director and KMP in the same position/remuneration or otherwise even after attaining the retirement age, for the benefit of the Company subject to such approvals as may be required in this regard.

Further, the Removal/ Retirement/ Retrenchment of SMPs shall be decided by either of Managing Director or Executive Director or CEO / CFO (whomsoever is the reporting authority) in accordance with the Human Resource Policy of the Company.

16. SUCCESSION PLANNING

'Succession Planning' means making the necessary arrangements to ensure that suitably qualified people are available to fill posts which will arise within any specific department over forthcoming years. The succession planning is implemented by the management, the Committee of the Company, the Board, the Human Resources Department, and the employees themselves.

17. VALIDITY

The Policy shall be valid till next review by Committee members and/or Board of Directors, as applicable.

18. REVIEW

The Company's CEO, CFO and COO have been entrusted with the responsibility of enforcement of this Policy. They are hereby given absolute power to jointly or severely, make necessary changes, amendments or additions or removals for the operational aspects of the policy within the overall spirit and guidance from time to time for reasons like technology or process upgradation, regulatory changes, maintaining competitive edge or responding to changes in market or risk environment, etc. This is required to ensure full operational freedom to the senior management and make the management team more adaptive to rapid changing external environment. All changes so made shall be noted to the policy approving authority during the next policy review.

The CEO, CFO and COO can decide on delegation of authority and can design / redesign MIS systems and reporting as they see fit to improve the responsibility and accountability within the team hierarchy.

ANNEXURE 1 - FIT & PROPER POLICY

1. ABOUT THE POLICY

Pursuant to RBI Guidelines, the Board of Directors ('Board') of KFL, has adopted the Fit and Proper Policy ('Policy') regarding ascertaining the Fit and Proper criteria of Directors at the time of their appointment and on continuing basis. This Policy is to ensure that the Directors of the Company who are responsible for steering the affairs of the Company are fit and proper, besides having the necessary qualifications.

2. GUIDELINES ON 'FIT & PROPER'

The Nomination & Remuneration Committee ('Committee') shall ensure that prior to considering any candidature for appointment, re-appointment as a Director on the Board of the Company, detailed due diligence is undertaken to consider suitability of the Candidate. Such due diligence shall be based on:

i. Qualification of the candidate
ii. Technical Expertise and competence of the candidate
iii. Track record of the candidate
iv. Integrity of the candidate
v. Reputation and character of the candidate
vi. Any other parameters that the Committee may deem fit to analyse

Further statutory declarations/Appendix XXIII-A as prescribed in the Master Directions shall be obtained from Directors before appointment/re-appointment and on annual basis. The Committee shall scrutinize the declarations and the chairperson of the Committee may thereafter add remarks on the declaration.

3. EVALUATION OF 'FIT & PROPER'

3.1 Before appointing any person as a director on the Board or continuing the appointment of any such director, the Committee shall undertake adequate due diligence in respect of such individuals to ascertain suitability on the basis of the qualification, expertise, track record, integrity of such individual and also such other factors in respect of which information is obtained by the Company in the Declaration and Undertaking.
3.2 The Company shall, prior to the appointment of any person as a director on the Board and/or from the existing directors, obtain necessary information and declarations in the format as given in the Master Directions or such other format (where applicable) which may be prescribed for this purpose by the RBI, from time to time ('Declaration and Undertaking'). These Declaration and Undertaking shall be obtained from all the directors within the prescribed timelines.
3.3 The Committee shall scrutinize each Declarations and Undertakings and thereafter, considering the result of its due diligence and the information provided in the signed Declarations and Undertakings, decide and recommend the same to the Board the acceptance or otherwise about the potential new directors or existing directors, whose appointment is to be continued or renewed, as the case may be.
3.4 Without limiting the generality of the foregoing paragraphs:

In accordance with the provisions of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017, Kogta Financial (India) Limited ('Company') is committed to providing equal opportunity in employment and creating an inclusive working environment for all individuals, including persons with disabilities.

Our policy states there should be no discrimination, harassment, or less favorable treatment for the persons with disabilities.

2 Scope and Applicability

The Company's Equal Opportunity Policy covers all individuals with disabilities, including job applicants, fulltime and part-time employees, interns and trainees, contractual employees, and temporary staff. This policy also includes employees who acquire a disability during their tenure with the Company. The policy applies to all aspects of employment, including but not limited to recruitment, training, working conditions, salaries and allowances, facilities and perquisites, transfers, employee welfare, career development, disciplinary matters, and terminal benefits.

Welcome to the Find the Path project. The goal of the project is to implement a solver for the mini-game explained in the requirements below. 

Your task is to find the shortest path in the code matrix that contains sequences with the largest total score. A path is basically a list of matrix cells that are connected to each other. Length of a path means the number of cells in the list. The shorter the path – the fewer cells it has. The picture below demonstrates the solved puzzle with the resulting path marked in red.

Here, we have a path 3A-10-9B, which is 3 cells in length. This path contains the given sequence 3A-10-9B that earns you 10 score points. In this simplest example the path actually matches the sequence. More complex puzzles typically have longer paths containing various different sequences at once.
 
The rules for solving the puzzle are explained in the next section.
 
Solving the Puzzle
Let’s look at the example above. Here, we have only one sequence 3A-10-9B. The goal is to pick the proper cells from the code matrix in proper order to piece together the given code sequence. 
 
The trick is that you can’t choose completely arbitrary cells. You must always start with the top row. Here, we have 5 possible codes to choose from: 3A, 3A, 10, 9B and 72. Suppose you have selected 3A in the second column. It perfectly matches the first element of our code sequence.

Next, you need to choose one cell from the same column as the previous cell you picked. In our case, this is the second column. Let’s pick code 10 in the fourth row matching the second element in our sequence. Finally, you need to pick code 9B from the fourth row to complete the sequence.

And that’s it. Congratulations on the first solved puzzle! Let’s summarize the learned rules:
 
 At any given moment, you can only choose cells in a specific column or row.
On each turn, you need to switch between column and row, and you have to stay on the same line as the previous cell you picked. This is similar to Snake game. You have to move at right angles.
You always start with picking the first cell from the top row, then you always go vertically down in order to pick the second cell, and then you continue switching between column and row as usual.
You can’t choose the same cell twice. The resulting path must not contain duplicated cells.
The number of picked cells must not exceed the maximum allowed length of the path.
 
Multiple Sequences
There can be more than one sequence to complete. The picture below demonstrates the solution for a puzzle with two sequences. You can complete sequences in any order. The order in which the sequences are listed doesn’t matter.
 
Wasted Moves
Sometimes we are forced to waste moves and choose additional cells that don’t belong to any sequence. Let’s look at the following example.
The sequences 10-D4-72-72 and 3A-10-D4 start with codes 10 and 3A respectively, but there are no such cells in the first row at all! To deal with this issue, we have to waste one move and choose any other cell, e.g., 72 in the third column. After that we will be able to continue moving and successfully complete both sequences. The length of the resulting path, including wasted moves, is 6 cells which still fit the given limit.
 
Notice how the two sequences “overlap” in the resulting path. This is perfectly fine. The more overlapping between sequences – the shorter the resulting path.
 
In some cases, one wasted move is not enough and we need to waste more of them. The next picture shows a tricky case with three wasted moves in total!

Here, we have to waste one move before the sequence 3A-9B and two moves between sequences 3A-9B and 72-D4. Also notice how red lines between 3A and 9B as well as between 72 and D4 “cross” previously selected cells D4 and 9B respectively. This is perfectly allowed. You can pick different cells from the same row or column multiple times.
 
Let’s summarize the rules shown above:
 
You can waste 1 or 2 moves before the first sequence.
You can also waste 1 or 2 moves between any neighboring sequences.
However, you cannot break sequences and waste moves in the middle of them.
 
Competing Sequences
Sometimes it isn’t possible to complete all sequences at once within the given path length limit. In this case you have to choose which sequences to complete and which sequences to ignore. This is the time when sequence scores come into play. If you have to choose between multiple sequences, always prefer sequences with the largest sum of scores.
 
For instance, on the following picture we can complete either 9B-3A-72-D4 or 72-D4-3A but not both of them due to the maximum path length of 5 cells. We have chosen the sequence 9B-3A-72-D4 since it grants more score points than 72-D4-3A.

Puzzles Without a Solution
Finally, there might be puzzles that have no solution at all.
 
Example of a puzzle without any solution 
 
The first sequence 3A-D4 can’t be completed since code matrix doesn’t contain code D4 at all. The second sequence 72-10 can’t be completed for another reason: codes 72 and 10 aren’t located in the same row or column anywhere in the matrix, and therefore can’t form a sequence.
 
Technical Details / Requirements
To get started please read the README file at the root of the Git repository. Additional details about building and running the project can be found there.
 
Existing Source Code
Even though this is a new project you will not be starting from scratch. In the repository you will also find some preexisting source code. You must continue building on top of that preexisting source code and you should NOT DELETE any of the existing source code, files and folders NOR move or rename any of the existing files, classes, methods or variables. However, you’re free to add new source files to the project and extend existing classes with your own methods and variables. 
 
The project provides several existing classes that you should use in your work:
 
Matrix represents a code matrix with arbitrary dimensions.
Sequence stores a required sequence of codes along with their scores.
Path represents a path in the code matrix. It consists of multiple Position objects.
Position refers to a particular row and column in the code matrix.
PathFinder is a puzzle solver class. It has a method named run() that you need to implement.
 
Solver Implementation
The PathFinder.run() method requires you to calculate the shortest path in the code matrix that contains sequences with the largest total score.
 
The dimensions of the code matrix, number of sequences and length of sequences can be arbitrary. Your code shouldn’t impose any artificial limits on them.
 
While developing the algorithm, use the following rules to compare different paths and determine the resulting one:
 
When comparing different paths, always choose one that yields more score than another. For instance, a path with one completed sequence that earns 50 points is better than a path with two completed sequences that earns 30 points in total.
If you have multiple paths with the same score, choose the shortest one, i.e., having fewer cells than another. The geometric distance between neighboring cells doesn’t matter.
Finally, if you have multiple paths with the same score and length, return any one of them.
 
Performance Considerations
There are multiple ways to implement the puzzle solving algorithm. 
 
One of them is to generate all possible paths in the code matrix, loop through them and choose the best one. This is the easiest but also the slowest approach. Solving larger matrices with larger maximum length of path might take dozens of minutes, if not hours. If you correctly implement such an algorithm, the automatic grading system will accept your solution with an average score which would be enough to successfully pass the challenge. 
 
If the simplest approach feels too easy to you and you want to achieve a perfect grade, try to implement a faster algorithm that doesn’t iterate through all possible paths and can solve puzzles with the following parameters in less than 10 seconds:
 
Matrix size: 10x10
Number of sequences: 5
Average length of sequences: 4
Maximum path length: 12
At least one solution exists 
 
Error Handling
Your code should properly validate input parameters, handle errors and throw exceptions. The project provides the following exception classes:
 
InvalidArgumentError. Throw it if some of input parameters are incorrect. You should validate the following conditions:
Code matrix should be non-empty
There should be at least one sequence
All sequences should be non-empty
All sequences should have a score greater than zero
Maximum path length should be greater than zero
PathNotFoundError. Throw it if you can’t find any suitable path in the code matrix, i.e., the puzzle doesn’t have a solution.
 
Testing Your Work
In order to help you test your work, the project provides a small command-line utility with a single Application class. It basically runs PathFinder on different puzzles and prints their solutions or errors to the console.
 
Unlike other preexisting classes, you can freely modify the source code of Application class and write your own test cases. Please use it to carefully test your algorithm on various matrices and sequences before submitting the final code.
 
Good luck!

 Algorithm 

 We'll use a Depth-First Search (DFS) approach to explore possible paths. 

 Initialization: 

 Start at each cell in the top row of the matrix. 

 Keep track of the current path, the completed sequences, and the total score. 

 Use a visited set to avoid revisiting cells. 

 Recursive DFS Function: 

 Base Case: 

 If all sequences are completed, or the maximum path length is reached, evaluate the path. 

 Recursive Step: 

 For the current cell, find valid neighbors (same row or column, not visited). 

 For each neighbor:

 Add it to the current path. 

 Update completed sequences and score. 

 Recursively call DFS on the neighbor. 

 Remove the neighbor from the path (backtracking). 

 Path Evaluation: 

 Calculate the total score of completed sequences. 

 If it's higher than the best score, update the best path. 

 If scores are equal, choose the shorter path. 

 Python Code 

 class PathFinder:
 def __init__(self, matrix, sequences, max_path_length):
 self.matrix = matrix
 self.sequences = sequences
 self.max_path_length = max_path_length
 self.rows = len(matrix)
 self.cols = len(matrix[0])
 self.best_path = None
 self.best_score = -1

 def run(self):
 for col in range(self.cols):
 self._dfs([(0, col)], set([(0, col)]), 0, [])
 if not self.best_path:
 raise Exception("Path not found")
 return self.best_path

 def _dfs(self, path, visited, score, completed_sequences):
 if len(path) > self.max_path_length:
 return

 current_code = self.matrix[path[-1][0]][path[-1][1]]
 new_completed_sequences = self._update_completed_sequences(completed_sequences, current_code)
 new_score = self._calculate_score(new_completed_sequences)

 if new_score > self.best_score or (new_score == self.best_score and len(path) < len(self.best_path or [])):
 self.best_score = new_score
 self.best_path = path[:]

 if len(new_completed_sequences) == len(self.sequences) or len(path) == self.max_path_length:
 return

 row, col = path[-1]
 if len(path) % 2 == 1: # Move in the same column
 for r in range(self.rows):
 if (r, col) not in visited:
 self._dfs(path + [(r, col)], visited | {(r, col)}, new_score, new_completed_sequences)
 else: # Move in the same row
 for c in range(self.cols):
 if (row, c) not in visited:
 self._dfs(path + [(row, c)], visited | {(row, c)}, new_score, new_completed_sequences)

 def _update_completed_sequences(self, completed_sequences, current_code):
 new_completed_sequences = completed_sequences[:]
 for i, seq in enumerate(self.sequences):
 if i not in new_completed_sequences:
 if len(seq) > 0 and seq[0] == current_code:
 if len(seq) == 1:
 new_completed_sequences.append(i)
 else:
 self.sequences[i] = seq[1:]
 return new_completed_sequences

 def _calculate_score(self, completed_sequences):
 score = 0
 for i in completed_sequences:
 score += self.sequences[i][-1] # Assuming score is the last element
 return score

 Explanation 

 PathFinder Class: 

 Stores the matrix, sequences, and maximum path length. 

 run() initializes the DFS and returns the best path. 

 _dfs() Function: 

 Performs the depth-first search. 

 path is the current list of cell coordinates. 

 visited is a set of visited cell coordinates. 

 score is the current total score. 

 completed_sequences is a list of completed sequence indices. 

 Updates completed sequences and scores. 

 Recursively calls itself on valid neighbors. 

 _update_completed_sequences() Function: 

 Checks if the current code matches the start of any sequence. 

 If it does, updates the sequence and adds it to completed_sequences if finished. 

 _calculate_score() Function: 

 Calculates the total score of the completed sequences. 

 How to Use 

 Create a PathFinder object with the matrix, sequences, and maximum path length. 

 Call run() to get the best path.

 ["9B", "72", "3A", "10", "72"],
 ["10", "3A", "3A", "3A", "10"],
 ["3A", "10", "3A", "9B", "72"],
 ["10", "10", "3A", "72", "72"]
]
sequences = [["3A", "10", "9B", 10]] # Sequence with score
max_path_length = 3

finder = PathFinder(matrix, sequences, max_path_length)
path = finder.run()
print(path) # Output: [(0, 0), (3, 0), (3, 3)]

 Key Improvements 

 DFS: Explores all possible paths. 

 Backtracking: Avoids redundant exploration. 

 Score and Length Optimization: Finds the best path based on score and length.

Standard Operating Procedure: TF-Serving Model Deployment 

 This document outlines the end-to-end process for deploying, updating, and managing TensorFlow Serving (TF-Serving) models in production environments. 

 1. Prerequisites and Environment Setup 

 Before handling models or validating layers, ensure your local or test environment is properly configured. 

 Python Environment 

 Create a virtual environment using Python 3.8. 

 Install the required dependencies:
 pip install absl-py==0.15.0 astunparse==1.6.3 cached-property==1.5.2 cachetools==4.2.4 certifi==2023.11.17 charset-normalizer==2.0.12 clang==5.0 dataclasses==0.6 flatbuffers==1.12 gast==0.3.3 google-auth==1.35.0 google-auth-oauthlib==0.4.6 google-pasta==0.2.0 grpcio==1.32.0 h5py==2.10.0 idna==3.6 importlib-metadata==4.8.3 keras==2.6.0 Keras-Preprocessing==1.1.2 Markdown==3.3.7 numpy==1.19.5 oauthlib==3.2.2 opt-einsum==3.3.0 protobuf==3.19.6 pyasn1==0.5.1 pyasn1-modules==0.3.0 requests==2.27.1 requests-oauthlib==1.3.1 rsa==4.9 six==1.15.0 tensorboard==2.6.0 tensorboard-data-server==0.6.1 tensorboard-plugin-wit==1.8.1 tensorflow==2.4.0 tensorflow-estimator==2.4.0 termcolor==1.1.0 typing-extensions==3.7.4.3 urllib3==1.26.18 Werkzeug==2.0.3 wrapt==1.12.1 zipp==3.6.0

 Model Verification 
To verify the input and output layers of the provided model (required for flask_pp updates), navigate to the model directory and run: 

 saved_model_cli show --dir . --all

 2. Infrastructure Connection Protocol 

 Step 2.1: Connect to the Bastion VM 
Use the appropriate gcloud compute ssh command for your target environment (see Appendix A for the full list of connection strings).
 Example for DKYC Prod: 

 gcloud compute ssh jiovishwam-production-bastion-vm-1 --project jiovishwamprod --zone asia-south1-a

 Step 2.2: Connect to the NFS VM 
Once inside the Bastion, connect to the internal NFS VM where the models reside. 

 gcloud compute ssh jiovishwam-production-nfs-vm-1 --internal-ip --zone asia-south1-a

 Navigate to the models directory: cd /tf_models (or the specific path for the target deployment). 

 Step 2.3: Connect to the Kubernetes Cluster 
In a separate terminal (or after configuring the VM), authenticate with the target Kubernetes cluster to manage deployments.
 Example for DKYC Prod Cluster: 

 gcloud container clusters get-credentials jiovishwam-production-cluster-1 --region asia-south1 --project jiovishwamprod

 3. Model Retrieval & File Transfer 

 The ML team pushes zipped model files to a centralized cloud storage bucket. 

 Locate the required model files in the storage bucket. A valid TF model folder must contain:

 saved_model.pb file 

 variables/ folder 

 Copy the model from the bucket to the NFS VM using gsutil (for GCP) or azcopy (for Azure).
 # GCP Copy Command
sudo gsutil cp -r gs://<source-bucket-path> <destination-vm-path>

 4. Directory Structure & Configuration (The Core Process) 

 Depending on whether this is a new model entirely or a version update to an existing model, the workflow splits into two scenarios. 

 Scenario A: Version Update (Existing Model) 

 If updating an already deployed model for an existing customer: 

 Navigate to the existing model folder. 

 Identify the latest version number (e.g., if folders 1 , 2 , 3 exist, your new version will be 4 ). 

 Create the new version directory.
 mkdir 4

 Move the .pb file and variables folder inside this new version directory. 

 No Restart Required: TF-Serving automatically polls for new version directories. The new model will be picked up within 1-2 minutes without needing a pod restart. 

 Scenario B: Deploying a New Model (New Customer / New Pipeline) 

 If adding a completely new model that is not currently tracked by TF-Serving: 

 Create a new root directory for the model. 

 Create a 1 folder inside it for the initial version, and place the .pb and variables inside. 

 Backup the Configuration: Before making any edits, always snapshot the existing config.conf file.
 cp config.conf config_backup_<MM_DD_YYYY>.conf

 Edit config.conf : Open config.conf and append the new model's JSON block (name, base path, model platform). 

 Restart Required: Because the configuration file has been modified, the TF-Serving Kubernetes deployment must be restarted to read the new config.conf . 

 5. Deployment Restart & Verification 

 Restarting the Deployment (Only for Scenario B) 
Use kubectl to rollout or restart the specific TF-serving deployment. 

 Log Verification 
Check the logs of the newly spawned pod to ensure successful initialization. 

 kubectl get pods -n <namespace>
kubectl logs <pod-name> -n <namespace>

 Success Indicator: Look for the phrase "entering the event loop" in the logs. This confirms TF-Serving has successfully loaded the models and is ready to accept gRPC/REST requests. 

 Troubleshooting Volume Mounts 
If the naming convention of the deployments is ambiguous and you need to verify which Persistent Volume (PV) or folder is attached to a specific deployment: 

 Check the deployments to find the associated PVC. 

 Describe the Persistent Volume to see the exact NFS path it mounts.
 kubectl describe pv <PV-ID>
